courseDetails.title: Introduction to Web Technologies
courseDetails.description: A 100-level course covering the Internet and World Wide Web, web protocols, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, the DOM, libraries and frameworks, PHP, backend development, security, deployment, and emerging web technologies.

questions.question: Which statement best defines web development?
options: The practice of managing telephone networks
The design of printed documents without digital content
The process of repairing only computer hardware
The process of creating websites and web applications for the Internet
questions.explanation: Web development covers the creation of websites and web applications, including front-end interfaces and back-end logic.

questions.question: A developer is responsible for the layout, colours, navigation, and visible interaction of an online store. Which role is being performed?
questions.explanation: Front-end development focuses on the user interface and the visual and interactive parts seen in the browser.

questions.question: What is the primary role of a web browser?
options: To interpret and display web content for the user
To store every website permanently on the user's device
questions.explanation: A browser interprets resources such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and renders them in a user-friendly form.

questions.question: Which task is normally performed by a web server?
options: Processing client requests and returning requested web resources
Providing keyboard input directly to the browser
Drawing every page manually on the user's monitor
Converting all websites into desktop applications
questions.explanation: A web server receives requests, locates or generates resources, and sends responses to clients.

questions.question: A user clicks a link in a browser. Which sequence correctly describes the client-server interaction that follows?
options: The server sends a request to the browser before the user acts
The database sends CSS directly to the monitor without a response
The browser sends an HTTP request, the server processes it and returns a response, and the browser renders the content
The browser renders the page before contacting any server
questions.explanation: The client initiates the request, the server processes it and responds, and the browser displays the returned resources.

questions.question: What does a Uniform Resource Locator identify?
options: The programming language used by a database
The location or address of a web resource
The colour scheme of a website
The amount of memory in a server
questions.explanation: A URL is the web address used to locate a resource such as a page, image, or file.

questions.question: A team wants to track code changes, create feature branches, and restore an earlier version when necessary. Which tool category is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Version control systems such as Git preserve change history and support branching, merging, rollback, and collaboration.

questions.question: A server placed between users and backend servers caches common responses and distributes traffic. What type of server is it?
questions.explanation: Proxy servers act as intermediaries and may provide caching, load balancing, and security filtering.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a markup language?
options: To structure and describe data or document content using tags or elements
To compress all network packets automatically
To control electrical power supplied to a server
questions.explanation: Markup languages provide a standard way to describe document structure and data so that humans and machines can interpret it.

questions.question: Which markup language is designed mainly for storing and exchanging structured data with user-defined tags?
questions.explanation: XML represents structured data hierarchically and allows developers to define descriptive tags.

questions.question: A logo must remain sharp when enlarged from a phone screen to a large display. Which format from the course is most suitable?
options: A raster screenshot stored as unstructured text
questions.explanation: SVG describes vector graphics, so the image can scale without losing quality.

questions.question: Which markup language is specifically intended for mathematical notation and equations on web pages?
questions.explanation: MathML is an XML-based markup language for presenting mathematical expressions on the web.

questions.question: What is the main function of the Domain Name System?
options: Translating domain names into IP addresses
Executing PHP directly in the browser
Encrypting every file stored on a computer
questions.explanation: DNS resolution maps human-readable domain names to the IP addresses used to locate hosts.

questions.question: Which protocol is primarily used to send outgoing email between mail systems?
questions.explanation: SMTP handles the sending and relaying of email, while POP3 and IMAP are used mainly for retrieving messages.

questions.question: A web application needs a persistent two-way connection so that the server can push live updates to the browser. Which technology best fits this need?
questions.explanation: WebSocket supports persistent, full-duplex communication between a client and server.

questions.question: A developer must transfer a confidential configuration file while encrypting both credentials and file contents. Which protocol should be used?
questions.explanation: SFTP transfers files through a secure encrypted connection, unlike ordinary FTP.

questions.question: Which HTML declaration tells the browser that a document uses HTML5?
questions.explanation: The HTML5 doctype is written as <!DOCTYPE html> at the beginning of the document.

questions.question: Which HTML section normally contains metadata and the page title rather than visible page content?
questions.explanation: The head stores metadata, links to resources, and the title; visible document content is mainly placed in the body.

questions.question: A developer wants to embed a product photograph in a page. Which HTML element should be used?
questions.explanation: The element embeds an image, with the source usually specified through its src attribute.

questions.question: Which HTML element groups input controls and defines how their data is submitted?
questions.explanation: The form element contains controls and uses attributes such as action and method to define submission behaviour.

questions.question: Which attribute of an anchor element specifies the destination of a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The href attribute contains the URL or target to which an anchor link navigates.

questions.question: A website needs a list of product features that can be scanned quickly, but their order is not important. Which structure is most semantic?
questions.explanation: An unordered list represents a collection of items where sequence does not carry meaning.

questions.question: What is the key difference between GET and POST form submission?
options: GET always encrypts data, while POST never can
GET commonly places submitted data in the URL, while POST sends it in the request body
GET is a CSS property, while POST is an HTML heading
questions.explanation: GET parameters are commonly visible in the query string; POST carries form data in the request body.

questions.question: Which HTML5 attribute can make a form field impossible to submit when it is left empty?
questions.explanation: The required validation attribute tells the browser that the field must contain a value before submission.

questions.question: Why should an image used for meaningful content include an alt attribute?
options: To change the HTTP method to POST
To provide a text alternative for accessibility and unavailable images
questions.explanation: Alternative text helps screen-reader users and provides meaning when the image cannot be displayed.

questions.question: Which CSS selector targets every element with class="notice"?
questions.explanation: A class selector begins with a period, so .notice selects elements whose class includes notice.

questions.question: Which CSS selector targets the single element whose id is mainHeader?
questions.explanation: An ID selector begins with # and matches the element carrying that id value.

questions.question: Padding, border, and margin are being adjusted around a paragraph. Which CSS concept is involved?
questions.explanation: The CSS box model consists of content, padding, border, and margin.

questions.question: Which part of the CSS box model creates space between the content and its border?
questions.explanation: Padding is the internal space between an element's content and border; margin is outside the border.

questions.question: A developer wants items in a navigation bar arranged in one flexible row with controlled spacing. Which CSS layout is especially suitable?
questions.explanation: Flexbox is designed for one-dimensional alignment and distribution of items along a row or column.

questions.question: Which Flexbox property distributes items along the main axis?
questions.explanation: justify-content controls alignment and spacing of flex items along the container's main axis.

questions.question: Which CSS feature applies different style rules according to conditions such as screen width?
questions.explanation: Media queries are central to responsive design because they apply styles under specified device or viewport conditions.

questions.question: Which unit is relative to the root element's font size?
questions.explanation: The rem unit is calculated relative to the root element's font size.

questions.question: A page needs a two-dimensional arrangement of rows and columns. Which CSS system is most appropriate?
options: Flexbox used only as an email protocol
questions.explanation: CSS Grid is designed for two-dimensional layouts involving both rows and columns.

questions.question: What is JavaScript's primary role in client-side web development?
options: Adding behaviour and interactivity to web pages in the browser
questions.explanation: JavaScript executes in the browser to respond to users, modify content, validate input, and perform dynamic operations.

questions.question: Which declaration creates a block-scoped variable whose value may later be reassigned?
questions.explanation: let creates a block-scoped variable and permits reassignment, unlike const.

questions.question: What does the JavaScript operator === check?
options: Whether one number is greater than another
Equality of both value and data type
Only whether two variable names are spelled alike
questions.explanation: Strict equality compares both value and type, unlike ==, which may perform type conversion.

questions.question: Which loop is most suitable when the number of repetitions is known in advance?
questions.explanation: A for loop conveniently combines initialisation, a condition, and an update for a known iteration pattern.

questions.question: What is a closure in JavaScript?
options: A command that deletes every global variable
A tag that closes an HTML document
A function that retains access to variables from its surrounding lexical scope
A protocol for closing an FTP session
questions.explanation: A closure allows a function to continue using variables from the scope in which it was created.

questions.question: Which array method adds one or more elements to the end of an array?
questions.explanation: push() appends elements to the end, while pop() removes the final element.

questions.question: Which array method creates a new array containing only elements that satisfy a test?
questions.explanation: filter() evaluates each element and returns a new array of those for which the test is true.

questions.question: A student object has a property named score. Which expression correctly reads it using dot notation?
questions.explanation: JavaScript object properties can be accessed with dot notation as object.property.

questions.question: An online calculator must update its result immediately whenever the user types. Which technology directly enables this client-side behaviour?
options: A server process that runs only after final submission
A database query required for every keystroke
questions.explanation: Browser-side JavaScript can listen for input and recalculate instantly without a page reload.

questions.question: A second dropdown must update as soon as a user selects a category in the first dropdown. Which event is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: The change event fires when the selected value of a form control changes.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of client-side form validation?
options: To guarantee that server-side validation is unnecessary
To replace the form element with a database
To detect invalid input and give feedback before data is submitted
questions.explanation: Client-side validation improves usability, but server-side validation is still needed for security and reliability.

questions.question: Which technique allows a page to send or receive data without performing a full page reload?
questions.explanation: AJAX enables asynchronous communication with a server and dynamic updates to part of a page.

questions.question: What does a JavaScript Promise represent?
options: The eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation
A CSS rule that must always be applied
questions.explanation: A Promise provides a structured way to handle a future result or error from asynchronous work.

questions.question: Why is async/await commonly used?
options: To write Promise-based asynchronous code in a clearer sequential style
To make HTML tags execute as PHP
questions.explanation: async and await make asynchronous control flow easier to read while still using Promises.

questions.question: What is the role of the JavaScript event loop?
options: Coordinating execution of queued callbacks and asynchronous tasks without blocking the main flow
Translating domain names to IP addresses
questions.explanation: The event loop checks task queues and schedules callbacks when the call stack is available.

questions.question: Which modern JavaScript syntax inserts expressions directly inside a backtick-delimited string?
questions.explanation: Template literals use backticks and ${...} placeholders to embed expressions in strings.

questions.question: Which browser API provides a Promise-based way to make network requests?
questions.explanation: The Fetch API returns a Promise and is commonly used for asynchronous HTTP requests.

questions.question: What does the Document Object Model represent?
options: A hierarchical, programmable representation of an HTML or XML document
A CSS file stored outside the page
The unchangeable original source text only
questions.explanation: The DOM models a document as nodes and objects that scripts can inspect and modify.

questions.question: Which DOM method directly selects an element by its unique id?
questions.explanation: getElementById() returns the element whose id matches the supplied value.

questions.question: Which property is generally safest when changing only the text displayed inside an element?
options: innerHTML when arbitrary user input is inserted
questions.explanation: textContent sets plain text and does not interpret it as HTML markup.

questions.question: When is innerHTML appropriate?
options: When uploading a file through SFTP
When trusted HTML markup must be inserted or replaced inside an element
questions.explanation: innerHTML parses a string as markup, so it should be used carefully and not with untrusted content.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly creates a new paragraph and places it inside a container?
options: Declare it with SQL and send it through POP3
Use only a CSS selector without creating a node
Create it with fetch() and style it with SMTP
Create it with document.createElement() and insert it with appendChild() or append()
questions.explanation: DOM creation and insertion are separate steps: create a node, set its content, and append it to a parent.

questions.question: How can JavaScript respond when a user clicks a button?
options: Add a PHP opening tag to the CSS file
Attach a click event listener to the button
questions.explanation: An event listener runs a specified handler when the target event occurs.

questions.question: What are data-* attributes primarily used for?
options: Replacing class and id selectors entirely
Storing custom data on HTML elements for access through the dataset API
questions.explanation: Custom data attributes associate extra information with elements and are exposed through element.dataset.

questions.question: A script removes a completed task from a to-do list. Which DOM operation is required?
options: Removing the corresponding element node from its parent
questions.explanation: Deleting a visible task from the DOM requires removing the node that represents it.

questions.question: What is the clearest distinction between a JavaScript library and a framework?
options: A framework cannot contain reusable code
Libraries always replace HTML and CSS
A library provides callable tools for particular tasks, while a framework supplies a broader application structure and controls the flow
A library runs only on servers, while a framework runs only in printers
questions.explanation: Libraries are usually selected and called as needed; frameworks impose conventions and an overall structure.

questions.question: A small site needs simplified DOM manipulation, animations, and AJAX without a full application framework. Which tool best matches the course material?
questions.explanation: jQuery is a lightweight JavaScript library known for DOM manipulation, events, AJAX, and animation.

questions.question: Which library is associated with utility functions for working with arrays, objects, and collections?
questions.explanation: Lodash supplies reusable utility functions and supports chaining for data manipulation.

questions.question: Which library discussed in the course focuses on parsing, formatting, and manipulating dates and times?
questions.explanation: Moment.js provides date parsing, formatting, arithmetic, timezone, and locale-related features.

questions.question: Which React feature reduces direct updates to the browser DOM by comparing an in-memory representation first?
questions.explanation: React uses a virtual DOM to calculate necessary changes before updating the actual DOM.

questions.question: Which Angular feature automatically synchronises data between the model and the user interface?
questions.explanation: Two-way data binding keeps model and interface values synchronised when either changes.

questions.question: Vue.js is described as progressively adoptable. What does this mean?
options: Developers can use as much or as little of it as a project requires
It can run only after every page is rewritten
It is restricted to database administration
questions.explanation: Vue can be introduced incrementally, from enhancing a small page section to building a complete application.

questions.question: In Express.js, what is middleware?
options: A function in the request-response pipeline that can inspect, modify, or pass control onward
An HTML comment placed in the head
A database column that stores passwords
A CSS unit between px and rem
questions.explanation: Express middleware executes in order and can perform tasks such as logging, authentication, parsing, or error handling.

questions.question: Where is PHP code normally executed in a web application?
options: Only within the user's monitor hardware
questions.explanation: PHP is a server-side scripting language; its output is sent to the client after execution.

questions.question: How does a PHP variable name begin?
questions.explanation: PHP variables are written with a leading dollar sign, such as $name.

questions.question: Which PHP operator joins two strings?
questions.explanation: PHP uses the dot operator to concatenate strings.

questions.question: Which PHP construct is most suitable when one value must be compared against several named cases?
questions.explanation: switch compares one expression with multiple case values and executes the matching block.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the break keyword inside a PHP switch case?
options: To terminate the web server permanently
To stop execution from continuing into later cases
To insert a line break in HTML automatically
questions.explanation: break exits the switch after the matched case, preventing unintended fall-through.

questions.question: Which keyword begins a custom function declaration in PHP?
questions.explanation: A PHP function declaration starts with the function keyword followed by its name and parentheses.

questions.question: What is the role of a return statement in a PHP function?
options: To send a computed value back to the caller
questions.explanation: return ends the function's current execution and supplies a value that the calling code can use.

questions.question: A recursive PHP function calculates factorials. What must it include to prevent endless self-calls?
options: A second web server for every call
questions.explanation: The base case defines when recursion stops; without it, calls may continue indefinitely.

questions.question: Which backend technology is highlighted as efficient for real-time applications because it runs JavaScript on the server?
questions.explanation: Node.js supports server-side JavaScript and event-driven applications such as real-time services.

questions.question: What does a server environment include?
options: Only the colour palette of the website
A single HTML paragraph with no infrastructure
The hardware, software, storage, operating system, and networking components needed to run services
questions.explanation: A server environment or stack combines the infrastructure and software required to host applications and data.

questions.question: Which database is a relational database management system commonly used for web applications?
questions.explanation: MySQL is an RDBMS used to store and query structured relational data.

questions.question: Which database from the course is document-oriented and suitable for large amounts of unstructured or semi-structured data?
questions.explanation: MongoDB is a NoSQL document database with a flexible schema.

questions.question: Why is Redis commonly used in web systems?
options: For fast in-memory caching, real-time analytics, and message brokering
questions.explanation: Redis is an in-memory key-value database suited to fast access and caching.

questions.question: What is database normalization intended to reduce?
options: Browser rendering speed by deleting CSS
The number of URLs in DNS
questions.explanation: Normalization organises relational data to avoid unnecessary duplication and update anomalies.

questions.question: What is an API endpoint?
options: The final pixel in an SVG image
A specific URL or URI through which an API exposes a resource or service
A local variable inside every function
A CSS declaration at the bottom of a file
questions.explanation: An endpoint is the address clients use to access a particular API operation or resource.

questions.question: Which practice is essential when integrating a third-party API?
options: Place secret keys in public HTML
Authenticate correctly, handle errors, respect limits, and test the integration
Assume every response is valid and ignore documentation
questions.explanation: Reliable API integration depends on correct authentication, testing, error handling, documentation, and secure credential management.

questions.question: What happens in an SQL injection attack?
options: A CSS class is applied twice
Malicious SQL is inserted through input to manipulate database operations
A browser enlarges an SVG image
An email is downloaded using IMAP
questions.explanation: SQL injection exploits unsafe database queries constructed from untrusted input.

questions.question: Which measure most directly reduces SQL injection risk?
options: Parameterized queries together with input validation
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries keep data separate from SQL commands, while validation rejects unacceptable input.

questions.question: What is cross-site scripting (XSS)?
options: The secure transfer of files through SFTP
The use of CSS across several pages
The distribution of traffic across servers
The injection of malicious script into content that runs in another user's browser
questions.explanation: XSS occurs when untrusted script reaches a page and executes in the victim's browser.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a Web Application Firewall?
options: To act as a JavaScript array
To inspect and filter HTTP or HTTPS traffic before it reaches the web application
questions.explanation: A WAF helps block suspicious web requests and common application-layer attacks.

questions.question: Which hosting option places an organisation's servers within its own physical facilities?
questions.explanation: On-premises hosting means the organisation owns or manages the servers at its own site.

questions.question: What is horizontal scaling?
options: Adding more server instances to share the workload
Adding more columns to an HTML table
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling expands capacity by adding machines or instances rather than only upgrading one server.

questions.question: Why is load balancing used?
options: To download email from a server
To combine all passwords into one field
To distribute incoming requests across multiple servers and avoid a single bottleneck
questions.explanation: A load balancer improves availability and performance by spreading traffic among healthy instances.

questions.question: How does caching improve web application performance?
options: It stores frequently used data or results so they can be returned without repeating expensive work
It changes domain names into CSS classes
It forces every request to recompute all data
It removes the need for security controls
questions.explanation: Caching reduces repeated processing and data access, often lowering response time and backend load.

questions.question: Which development practice automatically runs tests when code changes are integrated into a shared repository?
questions.explanation: Continuous integration regularly combines code changes and runs automated checks to detect problems early.

questions.question: Why is WebAssembly useful for computationally intensive browser applications?
options: It replaces the Internet with a local printer
It can execute compiled code in the browser at near-native performance
It is only a CSS naming convention
questions.explanation: WebAssembly enables high-performance browser workloads such as games, simulations, and media processing.

questions.question: What characterises serverless architecture?
options: The cloud provider manages infrastructure while developers deploy functions or services
Every function must run in the user's CSS file
questions.explanation: Serverless hides server management from developers; the provider still operates the underlying infrastructure.

questions.question: A shopping site automatically increases computing capacity during a holiday traffic surge and reduces it afterward. Which serverless benefit is illustrated?
options: Manual DNS entry for every customer
questions.explanation: Serverless platforms can scale functions in response to demand and reduce resources when traffic falls.

questions.question: Which web trend uses learned patterns to provide recommendations, predictions, or intelligent interactions?
options: Machine learning and artificial intelligence on the web
questions.explanation: ML and AI can analyse data to power recommendations, computer vision, language tools, and predictive services.

questions.question: What is edge AI?
options: Applying a border to an HTML element
Placing every database at the centre of one page
Running AI processing closer to where data is generated to reduce latency
Using only email attachments for computation
questions.explanation: Edge AI processes data near devices or users rather than relying entirely on a distant central service.

questions.question: Which accessibility principle requires information and interface components to be presented in forms users can perceive?
questions.explanation: Perceivable content includes alternatives and presentations that users with different abilities can sense.

questions.question: Which assistive technology converts page text and interface information into speech or Braille?
questions.explanation: Screen readers help blind and visually impaired users access digital content through speech or Braille output.

questions.question: What is a Progressive Web App intended to combine?
options: Static pages that cannot work on mobile devices
Only server hardware and database cables
The reach of the web with app-like features such as responsiveness, installability, and offline support
questions.explanation: PWAs use modern web capabilities to provide reliable, responsive, and app-like experiences across devices.
